answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to post a costly non-transferable stake before it can earn, like an opal locked away as collateral: spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive because every fake must fund its own stake. Reputation then grows slowly like a vine, earned through verified work over time, so a fresh identity cannot instantly borrow trust. Rewards vest gradually like fruit in an orchard and are slashed if fraud is detected, so the attacker pays upfront for each fake and loses the stake when caught.
